OCR/import issues are a direct cause of onboarding delays and quality failures, and they trigger additional support/remediation workload. Image-only scanned PDFs lack a text layer, so the standard PDF parser cannot extract text; without OCR pre-processing, ingestion fails or returns incomplete indexes, and TutorChat's citation accuracy drops below the go-live threshold (85% for Growth, 90% for Enterprise) [NL-031#NL-031-S04][NL-005#NL-005-S11]. As a result, tenants fail go-live validation, which extends onboarding timelines—OCR/scanned PDF issues account for 25% of onboarding delay incidents [NL-031#NL-031-S04][NL-012#NL-012-S06]. Examples include BrightPath Healthcare, which had the longest onboarding at 9.5 weeks due to scanned PDF compliance issues [NL-012#NL-012-S06][NL-031#NL-031-S04], and Northstar Financial, whose pilot kickoff was delayed three weeks while IT ran external OCR [NL-010#NL-010-S06]. Additionally, large OCR batches can block fast uploads in a shared queue (the March 14 outage cause was an import retry storm), degrading overall import/ingestion performance for all users [NL-021#NL-021-S06]. Failed onboardings trigger a mandatory remediation path—a 5-business-day corpus audit, customer content-owner cleanup, and potential escalation to the VP of Customer Success—and recurring blockers are reviewed monthly against onboarding metrics and support ticket patterns [NL-005#NL-005-S11]. In short, OCR/import deficiencies directly slow onboarding (worse citation accuracy, failed validation, longer timelines) and drive additional support/CS remediation effort.
